elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14.2 retains "Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer." Ownership was deliberately left with Vendor; only the licence sentence was upgraded.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in 14.1–14.3; Vendor ownership of Deliverables is preserved.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: 14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology," defined at 1.8 as Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines and connectors.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: 14.3: "To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies." The retained text expressly characterises the 13.2 licence as perpetual.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: 14.3 cross-refers to Section 13.2 but the text of 13.2 is not before me; the retained wording only states that licence is "perpetual" and says nothing about irrevocability.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Same cross-reference problem: Section 13.2's consideration terms are not in the cited or rendered text, so royalty-free status cannot be confirmed.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: 14.1: "As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services."

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: 14.1: "No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer." Securing, supporting and improving the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation; no resale, distribution or wider-purposes right is granted.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The rationale cites 14.4 as ruling out unilateral joint ownership, but 14.4 is not among the cited or rendered paragraphs; the rendered 14.1–14.3 text neither creates nor expressly negates joint ownership.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: 14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology" (1.8: pre-existing tools, models, templates, routines) and 1.4 excludes from Deliverables "generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel." Left intact by the redline.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14.2: "Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify, and sublicense each Deliverable for its business." The prior Order-Form-term expiry is deleted.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14.2 states the licence is "irrevocable"; the original "revocable" is removed, with no retained revocation or suspension hook in 14.1–14.3.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14.2 grants a licence "to use, modify, and sublicense each Deliverable for its business."

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14.2: "...and sublicense each Deliverable for its business"; the original "non-transferable" restriction is removed, so nothing retained contradicts the sublicence right.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: 14.1 (unchanged): processing rights are limited to "solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer" — service delivery only, no distribution, resale or wider-purposes right.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: all four licence modifiers (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free) plus use, modify and sublicense for Customer's business appear in a single rewritten sentence in 14.2, Vendor's ownership of Vendor Technology and know-how survives in 14.3/1.4, and the Customer Data processing limit in 14.1 is untouched. The finding is correctly scoped as a deviation resolved to the fallback.

The preferred level is not reached and was not claimed: Vendor still exclusively owns Deliverables with no assignment to Customer, and the irrevocable/royalty-free character of the embedded Vendor Technology licence depends on Section 13.2, which is not in evidence.

Minimality holds. Only the second sentence of 14.2 is rewritten; 14.1 and 14.3 are preserved verbatim, including the Customer-favourable identification and third-party-material approval duties. No survival tail, expense allocation, escrow, or procedural extras were added, and no words outside the fallback elements were deleted — the removed "revocable," "non-transferable" and term-expiry wording are precisely the terms that blocked elements 2, 3 and 7.

Intent is preserved. Vendor's ownership of Deliverables and Vendor Technology is intact, the 13.2 cross-reference in 14.3 still resolves, no defined term is orphaned, and no retained sentence contradicts the new grant (the only conflicting words — "revocable, non-transferable" and the Order Form term limit — were replaced rather than left standing).

Optional repair if the drafter wants to close the residual preferred-level gaps: confirm that Section 13.2 states the embedded Vendor Technology licence is irrevocable and royalty-free, and confirm Section 14.4 expressly bars joint ownership. Neither is required for the claimed fallback position.
